body.statement:
Put \(S=\alpha+\beta\), \(S_\star=d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), and \(D_\star=1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2S)\).  The bounded-overlap case now has the proved upper bound
\[
 R_n(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)
 \leq C\max\left\{n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},n^{-1/D_\star}\right\}
\]
and the exact oracle rate without a logarithmic multiplier when \(S\geq S_\star\).  Resolve the remaining frontier as follows.  When \(\kappa=0\) and \(S<S_\star\), determine whether the upper rate \(n^{-1/D_\star}\) is minimax sharp by constructing a matching full-support fixed-\(n\) Bernoulli product-mixture lower experiment on the exact uniform-design class, or derive the correct sharper lower rate.  When \(\kappa>0\), determine the explicit piecewise rate \(\rho_n(d,\kappa,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\), every critical logarithmic factor, a total data-only attaining estimator, a matching same-class lower experiment, and the necessary-and-sufficient partition for \(R_n\asymp R_n^e\) versus \(R_n/R_n^e\to\infty\).  No branch may assume smoothness of \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X]\), delete covariate support, or substitute an oracle submodel for the full class.

obligation.what_is_open: When \(\kappa=0\) and \(\alpha+\beta<S_\star\), only a matching exact-uniform nuisance-dominated lower bound, or a proof of a sharper replacement lower rate, remains open.  When \(\kappa>0\), the higher-order achievability bound, matching same-class converse, all critical logarithmic cases, and the necessary-and-sufficient oracle-penalty partition remain open.
obligation.obstruction: On the bounded-overlap slice, the new projection estimator settles the upper side, but the required fixed-\(n\) full-support product-mixture comparison is still absent: disjoint local bumps violate the \(\gamma\)-Holder contrast constraint below the elbow, overlapping frames violate partition locality and create shared-sign product terms, and filling transition holes contributes \(nh^d\delta^2\) at the candidate scale.  For \(\kappa>0\), rare-treatment weighting adds propensity-dependent projection and stabilization terms, while noninteger corner powers and max-norm tie surfaces obstruct the available smooth compensation constructions.
obligation.attempted: I completed the one-sided second-order construction at \(\kappa=0\): corrections to both \(Q\) and \(R\), exact Lebesgue Gram projection, the uniform \(h^\gamma\) contrast approximation, the \(\ell^{\alpha+\beta}\) and \(h^\gamma\ell^\alpha\) biases, and the nondegenerate and degenerate variance scales are all controlled.  I optimized bandwidth and rank to close the upper elbow.  Earlier lower-bound attempts using disjoint bumps, overlapping squared frames, and filled transition regions fail for the structural reasons in the obstruction and do not certify a nuisance converse.
obligation.partial_result:
Let \(S=\alpha+\beta\), \(S_\star=d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), and \(D_\star=1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2S)\).  On the exact bounded-overlap slice,
\[
 c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}
 \leq R_n(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)
 \leq C\max\left\{n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},n^{-1/D_\star}\right\},
 \qquad n\geq2.
\]
The upper side is attained by a total second-order projection R-learner with exact uniform-design Gram matrix, deterministic rank rounding, singular-value flooring, and clipping.  Consequently \(R_n\asymp R_n^e\asymp n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\) for \(S\geq S_\star\), with no logarithmic factor at equality.  For \(S<S_\star\), only the nuisance-dominated lower bound remains missing on this slice.  For \(\kappa>0\), the established fallback remains
\[
 c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}
 \leq R_n(d,\kappa,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)
 \leq C n^{-t/(2t+d+\kappa)},
 \qquad t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\},
\]
which is sharp when \(\alpha+\beta\geq\gamma\) but does not settle the rough-nuisance local-zero frontier.

body.justification: The remaining question now cleanly separates the missing exact-uniform converse below the bounded-overlap elbow from the still-undetermined local-zero frontier.
body.gap: No cited comparator supplies either the required full-support fixed-\(n\) lower experiment on the rough bounded-overlap slice or the complete Holder frontier at a propensity zero.
body.consumer: Resolving these branches would determine when weak local overlap and unknown propensity calibration create an information-theoretic penalty for pointwise CATE precision.
